sections.h2: What does the Madison County, NC Register of Deeds do for a home sale?
sections.html:
The register of deeds is the office that stamps a deed into the public record, which is the step that makes a transfer count against later buyers and lenders. In Madison County, North Carolina, you reach the office at 828-649-3131, according to the county's contact page.

The office is separate from the tax offices. It records the paper, collects the state's fixed recording fees and takes the deed excise tax before a deed goes on the books. Valuing the property and billing the yearly tax happens elsewhere, at the tax administration office in Marshall.

For a seller, the practical result is simple. Your closing attorney sends the signed deed here, the clerk checks it against format rules and fees, and recording fixes the order of priority. Ask the register of deeds for the current counter hours and street location before you drive over, or have your attorney record electronically.

sections.h2: Why does recording a deed matter in North Carolina?
sections.html:
An unrecorded deed does not protect the buyer against creditors or later purchasers who pay value. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease of more than three years, or right of first refusal only counts against those parties from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies.

Priority follows the time of registration, so the first instrument recorded generally wins over a later one. That is why a closing attorney records the deed and the new deed of trust the same day, in an order that matches the closing.

  • A deed that sits unrecorded leaves the buyer exposed to a judgment lien against the seller.
  • A deed of trust recorded late can fall behind other liens.
  • A deed recorded in the wrong county does not do the job.

Madison County parcels are recorded in Madison County even when the owner lives somewhere else. If a parcel crosses a county line, the excise tax goes to the county that holds the greater share of the value.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Madison County, NC?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets the same recording fees in every county by statute, so Madison County charges what G.S. 161-10 prints. A standard deed costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 for up to 35 pages.

State recording fees that apply at the Madison County register of deeds, as printed in G.S. 161-10
ItemFee
Instrument in general, first 15 pages$26.00
Each page over 15$4.00
Deed of trust or mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00
Each page over 35$4.00
Plat, per sheet$21.00
Certified copy, first page$5.00
Each additional certified page$2.00
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee

A document that does not meet the statute's formatting standards adds $25.00, and each additional instrument in one document adds $10.00. The statute calls the fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Source: G.S. 161-10.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Madison County seller pay?
sections.html:
The excise tax is $1.00 for each $500, or part of $500, of the price or value of the interest conveyed. The transferor pays it, which means the seller, and the register of deeds collects it before recording.

Half the money stays with the county general fund. The other half goes monthly to the state Department of Revenue, and the county may keep 2 percent of the state share. Ask your closing attorney for the exact figure on your settlement statement rather than estimating it, since it is tied to the stated consideration.

Because the seller owes the tax, it shows up as a line on the seller's side of the closing statement alongside any unpaid property tax and the payoff on a mortgage. If you sell to a cash buyer, the same tax applies, and it is deducted from your proceeds at the table.

sections.h2: Can Madison County deeds be recorded electronically or checked for fraud?
sections.html:
A March 2022 county newsletter announced a fraud detection service that emails you when a document matching a name you list is recorded in the Madison County Register of Deeds office. You sign up through a link and confirm by email, and the county warned that the message may land in a junk folder.

For an owner of land that stays in the family for years, an alert like that is useful. A forged deed or a fraudulent deed of trust shows up in the index the day it is recorded.

For filing the deed itself, ask the office which electronic recording vendors it accepts, and ask your closing attorney whether the closing will be recorded electronically.

sections.h2: How does the Madison County register of deeds connect to the tax office?
sections.html:
The two offices work from the same ownership facts, so a deed recorded in Marshall is what lets the assessor update the owner on the tax roll. The assessor's page says the office keeps up ownership changes and the property maps.

  • Record the deed first, then confirm the new owner name with Tax Administration at 828-649-0734.
  • Pay or credit the September 1 bill at closing so the lien does not follow the parcel.
  • If a circuit breaker deferral exists, the county asks attorneys for 10 days' notice to prepare deferred tax bills.
  • Get the parcel number from your tax bill so the deed and the tax record match.

Madison County had an estimated 22,553 residents on July 1, 2025 and 11,874 housing units. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 77.5 percent for 2020 to 2024, and the median value of an owner-occupied home at $284,600. A high share of owner-occupied homes means most deed work here is ordinary sales and family transfers.

sections.h2: What should a Madison County seller bring to recording?
sections.html:
Your attorney or title agent handles recording, but you can speed it up by having the pieces ready. The state sets the layout rules, and a deed that misses them costs the extra $25.00 nonstandard fee.

  • The signed and acknowledged deed with the grantor and grantee names spelled as on the prior deed.
  • The parcel identification number from the tax record.
  • The prior deed book and page reference, if you have it.
  • Payoff letters for any deed of trust, which the lender then cancels at no recording fee.

If the house came through an estate, the heirs often need court paperwork before the deed can be signed, and a small estate affidavit is filed with the clerk of superior court, not the register of deeds. A cash buyer can work around a messy chain of title, but the paperwork still has to be recorded.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Madison County, NC Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The county's contact page lists 828-649-3131 for the Register of Deeds. Call it to confirm the counter hours and which recording methods are accepted before you send a document.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Madison County, NC?
faqs.a: A standard deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for the first 35 pages. These are the uniform state fees in G.S. 161-10.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Madison County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The statute says the transferor pays the tax to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded, at $1.00 for each $500 of the consideration or part of $500.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Madison County?
faqs.a: No. North Carolina charges no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage, so your lender's release costs you nothing to file.

faqs.q: Does recording the deed change who gets the tax bill in Madison County?
faqs.a: Recording is what lets the assessor update the owner. After closing, confirm the new owner name with Tax Administration, and make sure the current year's September 1 bill is paid or credited at closing.
